1000956.etyen:
Ellipsis of jeg gratulerer deg med dagen (“I congratulate you on the day”). The expression contains gratulerer, the present indicative of gratulere (“to congratulate”), med (“with; on, concerning”), and dagen, the definite singular of dag (“day”).
The verb ultimately derives from Latin grātulārī (“to congratulate”), formed from Latin grātus (“pleasing, welcome; grateful”), from Proto-Italic *gʷrātos (“grateful”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʷr̥Htós (“praised”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʷerH- (“to welcome, praise”). a female given name; a variant of Nina, also used as a short form of names ending in -nine

1003004.etyen:
Variant of Nina (“female given name”). Nina is probably of Russian origin, either as a short form of Антонина (Antonina) or as a pet form belonging to the Anna name family.
Alternatively, Nine may be a short form of female given names ending in -nine, such as Anine. First attested in 1841; first documented in Sandefjord.
Under the Anna analysis, the name ultimately derives from Late Latin Anna (“female given name”), from Koine Greek Ἄννα (Ánna, “Anna”), from Biblical Hebrew חַנָּה (Ḥannāh, “Hannah; grace, favour”).
Compare Danish Nine and Swedish Nine (“female given name”).

1005052.etyen: A habitational surname from the Norwegian farm and place name Bø, with a silent final ⟨e⟩ reflecting older Danish orthography, in which a following ⟨e⟩ could indicate that the preceding vowel was long. The underlying place name is from the common noun bø (“farm; enclosed farmland, infield”), which derives from Old Norse bǿr (“farm, farmstead”), from the root of búa (“to dwell, reside”), from Proto-Germanic *būaną (“to dwell, reside”), ultimately from the Proto-Indo-European root *bʰuH- (“to be, grow”).
